# An async.query in a generic component, its answer's type the component's
# own parameter: a hook-like wrapper a program composes a cache from. The
# query leaves :pending and :failure unbound, so ImplicitState wraps it in a
# component of its own, which declared the cells at the types the call site
# bound -- here `asked`'s T and F, which no splice of `asked` then reached.
# bubbletea's cell was `*any`, and html's wrapper had no family. The wrapper
# is generic in its owner's parameters, and the owner's call binds them.
#
# The fetch waits on the script harness's server.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import async "sngl:async"
import http "sngl:http"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

// The length of `name`, asked of the script harness's server, which fails
// "bad" with a 500.
func lookup(name string, life async.Lifetime) async.Result[int] {
    match var r = http.get(url="http://127.0.0.1:47819/status/{name == "bad" ? 500 : 200}", life=life) {
        failed { return {failed=r} }
        ok {
            if r.status != 200 {
                return {failed={kind=async.FailureKind.server, message="no", code="{r.status}"}}
            }
            return {ok=name.length()}
        }
    }
}

// A query its caller hands the fetch, keeping the answer in `got`.
component asked[T any, F any](key string, fetch func(string, async.Lifetime) async.Result[T], :got option[T]) F {
    async.query(on=key, fetch=fetch, @load(v) { got = v })
}

component one ui.node {
    var length option[int] = null

    ui.vbox {
        asked(key="fig", fetch=lookup, :got=length)
        ui.text(value="{length}")
    }
}

func testAQueryInAGenericComponentAnswers(t test.Test, c one) {
    t.wait(func() => c.length != null, 5000)
    t.assert(c.length == 3)
}

// Answers kept by key, and why each that failed did.
struct Store[V any] {
    answers  map[string, V]
    failures map[string, string]
}

// Asks for `key` once the store has no answer for it, keeping what `keep`
// makes of the answer.
component cached[T any, V any, F any](key string, fetch func(string, async.Lifetime) async.Result[T], keep func(T) V, :store Store[V]) F {
    if !store.answers.contains(key) {
        async.query(on=key, fetch=fetch, @load(got) { store.answers[key] = keep(got) }, @fail(f) { store.failures[key] = f.message })
    }
}

component many ui.node {
    var lengths = Store[int]{answers={}, failures={}}

    ui.vbox {
        for var w = ["one", "three", "bad", "one"] {
            cached(key=w, fetch=lookup, keep=func(n int) => n * 10, :store=lengths)
        }
        ui.text(value="{lengths.answers.length()}")
    }
}

func testACacheOfQueriesKeepsEachAnswer(t test.Test, c many) {
    t.wait(func() => c.lengths.answers.length() == 2 && c.lengths.failures.length() == 1, 5000)
    t.assert(c.lengths.answers["three"] == 50 && c.lengths.answers["one"] == 30)
    t.assert(c.lengths.failures["bad"] == "no")
}

ui.window {
    one()
    many()
}
